title: Misattributed aggregate usage during shared-key failover
creator: Aisha Bhandari
description: Summary: During a cross-shard failover scenario where a shared API key is temporarily reassigned between edge shards, aggregate usage counters are occasionally misattributed to an unrelated org. The symptom is a short window (30s–2m) of inflated usage for the wrong tenant followed by later correction in reconciliation, which leads to transient overcharges and incorrect rate-limit enforcement. This ticket tracks investigation, mitigation, and a permanent fix.
impact_details: Observed on 2025-01-26 03:14–03:18 UTC: three customers reported spikes in daily token usage on their billing dashboards. Internal monitoring flagged per-org quota spikes for orgs that did not issue traffic. Reconciliation batch later moved most of the overcount to a transient internal 'unattributed' bucket, but downstream billing snapshot had already captured the inflated numbers for several invoices in progress.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Provision two edge shards (shard-A and shard-B) with shared key routing enabled.
2) Start a steady low-rate stream of requests from tenant-T using the shared key, pinned to shard-A.
3) Force shard-A to revoke leases and trigger failover to shard-B (simulate by killing the shard process).
4) Observe per-route and per-key aggregators during 0–2 minutes post-failover.
Expected: counters continue and remain attributed to tenant-T.
Observed: a portion of increments land in a temporary per-shard buffer that is reconciled with the wrong org id when shard-B replays buffered deltas.
investigation_notes:
- Initial traces show the per-key aggregator uses (org_id, key_id, epoch) tuples. During failover, a stale shard-local mapping table allowed buffered deltas to be stamped with an older org_id placeholder (NULL -> resolved to first mapped org in lookup table) when the mapping rpc to central config timed out.
- Redis stream consumer logs show duplicate XADD followed by an XREAD that returned two entries with the same client_request_id; deduplication logic only runs in the reconcile worker, so immediate enforcement observed incorrect counts.
- Clock skew between edge nodes and the reconciliation coordinator caused epoch boundary misclassification; boundary deltas were folded into the next epoch and applied under the temporary 'owner' annotation present in the shard-local cache.
- Repro surface narrowed to: shared API keys that are multi-tenant (shared across orgs) and shards operating under partial config (e.g., the shard has example.org -> key mapping but central config updates are pending).
- No evidence of data loss; increments are duplicated/misattributed rather than dropped.
recent_actions:
2025-01-29: Incident bridge (Aisha, Marco, Priya) — collected traces and logs.
2025-01-30: Hotfix deployed to hold replayed deltas in a quarantine queue until mapping confirmation from control plane (patch runtime-1.20-hotfix-qs).
2025-02-02: Added short-circuit in enforcement layer to consult canonical mapping in runtime metadata service when mapping fetch fails instead of falling back to local cache.
2025-02-08: Load-tested failover scenario in staging; reduced misattribution occurrences by ~90% but still see edge-case duplication in high-concurrency repros.
2025-02-11: Design review with PM and Security — agreed on full fix scope and risk assessment.
temporary_mitigation:
- Hold-and-quarantine replayed deltas during failover until control-plane confirmation (deployed).
- Increase reconciliation frequency to reduce exposure window from minutes to ~30s (config change).
- Alerting: new rule emits MISSING_MAPPING events when shard mapping rpc latencies exceed 200ms.
proposed_fix:
1) Remove fallback-to-first-org semantic: replayed deltas must be tagged with a definitive org_id or be quarantined and treated as 'unattributed'.
2) Introduce monotonic mapping-version stamped on every mapping; aggregators must include mapping_version with increments and enforcement must reject applies if versions mismatch by >1, triggering quarantine.
3) Move deduplication earlier: add idempotent write through Redis using client_request_id -> idempotency token TTL aligned with reconciliation windows.
4) Add strong unit/integration tests simulating concurrent failover + mapping update.
5) Backfill tool to correct any misattributed historical deltas before next billing cycle.
implementation_notes:
- Kernel components touched: edge-aggregator service, reconciliation-worker, mapping-rpc client, enforcement-layer.
- Data model: introduce mapping_version (integer) to per-key mapping record in central config; propagate via shard bootstrap.
- Storage: Redis streams will carry mapping_version in XADD payload; reconcile worker will treat entries lacking mapping_version as quarantined.
- Rollout plan: staged feature flag 'strict-mapping-version' initially off; enable for 5% traffic in dedicated after runtime-1.20 rollout, monitor for spurious denies.
- Backfill will use reconcile logs to identify suspect batches and reassign counts into 'correction' batch processed before invoicing cutoff.
risks_and_open_questions:
- Risk: strict mapping-version may increase transient rate-limit failures if control-plane mapping propagation is slow; need fast path for low-risk traffic.
- Q: What's acceptable SLA for quarantine latency before user-visible errors? PM suggests 30s.
- Q: Are there customers with long-lived multi-tenant shared keys where attribution semantics must remain as-is? Solutions engineering to flag customers.
- Risk: Backfill could alter already issued invoices; billing needs policy on corrections (credits vs retroactive adjustments).
next_steps:
1) Finalize schema change for mapping_version (Marco) — due 2025-02-14.
2) Implement idempotent Redis writes in edge-aggregator (Eng infra) — target 2025-02-18.
3) Build backfill/correction tool and coordinate with Billing (Priya) — prep by 2025-02-20.
4) Schedule staged rollout behind feature flag with tight observability (Aisha) — 2025-02-22.
5) Post-deploy 72h watch and SLO review, then enable broader ramp if no regressions.

final_resolution_criteria:
- No misattributions observed in canary for 48h at 5% traffic.
- Reconciliation shows zero net unexpected corrections over a 7-day window.
- Backfill tool ready and billing policy approved for adjustments.
- Feature flag fully rolled out and metrics within SLOs.
